security_problem: A registered agent that is later subverted can keep minting until TTL/depth/scope stop it. Removing the registry row is not the same as an explicit revocation signal, and already-minted next-hop tokens can still pass visor-gateway. Short-name matching would revoke the wrong agent.
required_behavior: serve and visor-gateway require -denylist (empty lists are valid). IDs match exactly. STS denies agent_id, attested workload, and verified principal when listed (agent_denied / workload_denied / principal_denied) and issues no token. visor-gateway denies the principal, acting agent, and every non-principal hop before any backend forward. SIGHUP loads registry, keys, and denylist then publishes one snapshot; an invalid denylist keeps the previous snapshot. visor-gateway re-reads the denylist on each verify.
failure_behavior: Fail closed: unknown fields, trailing JSON, empty IDs, duplicate IDs, non-URI agent/workload entries, aliased identity-file paths, and an unreadable denylist produce a process error or HTTP 503 with no mint and no backend forward.
